newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Prices rising on feedstock costs.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Prices rising on feedstock costs.

text.p: Tight supplies and high costs of feedstock are expected to push methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) spot prices in Asia up in the next few weeks, in spite of flat demand, industry sources said on Monday.
"Prices have been rather flat but the raw materials are increasing very sharply and we forecast an increasing trend... of maybe five percent," said a trader in Hong Kong.
Traders said MTBE cost-and-freight (c-and-f) to Singapore, the region's benchmark, has averaged $275 per tonne so far in 1997 but this week started to creep up towards $280.

MTBE producers said while feedstock butane was near 10-year high, they were more concerned about the price of methanol, another major component, which has risen in recent weeks by $80 per tonne to around $230.
"Methanol supplies are tight ... there are some problems with production in New Zealand and Labuan," said a producer. "So whatever is available is very expensive."
Although profit margins on MTBE production were under pressure, Asian producers said they were not following the U.S. where producers have been cutting output.

The main suppliers for Asia, Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) with an output of more than two million tonnes per year and MTBE Malaysia at 300,000 tonnes per year, have not cut throughputs, traders said.
Although demand is flat, it still outpaces current supplies.
Demand for MTBE for blending gasoline up to a higher octane level was weak. North Asian gasoline demand was low in the winter while the increase in South Korean refining capacity has reduced imports.
"There is no real blending demand, leaving most demand from countries where MTBE blending is mandated, such as Thailand and Taiwan," one trader said.

Fresh demand is mostly limited to Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC), which has issued a tender to buy up two 3,500-tonne cargoes for March 1-15 delivery after an absence from the market of two months. The tender closes January 22 and offers should be valid for two days.
An official said CPC had covered its January and February requirements, which ranged between four to six cargoes per month, with term commitments.
Traders said they expected to see higher awards for the March tender than the last tender for December, when awards were made at $275-$278 per tonne, c-and-f Taiwan.
Producers also expected a moderate rise in blending demand to meet CPC's tender to buy 95-octane unleaded reformate, which has a two percent MTBE content requirement.
The reformate tender seeks 250,000 barrels for March 1-15 delivery and closes January 28.
